hook.line: A smell, a song or a street can take you straight back to someone. Don Hernando says it with a small frame where the thing does the remembering.
hook.es: Ese olor a tinto me trae recuerdos de mi abuela.
hook.en: That smell of coffee brings back memories of my grandmother.

examples.es: Ese olor a tinto me trae recuerdos de mi abuela.
examples.en: That smell of coffee brings back memories of my grandmother.

examples.es: De repente me vino a la memoria su cara.
examples.en: Suddenly her face came to mind.

examples.es: Esta canción le trae muchos recuerdos a don Hernando.

examples.en: Now the name of the street comes to mind.

rule:
In Spanish, the thing does the bringing, and you are the one it happens to. It works like *gustar*.

*(Me, te, le, nos) trae(n) recuerdos de…* means "brings back memories of…". The thing is the subject: *ese olor me trae*, *estas canciones me traen*.

*Me viene a la memoria* means "it comes to mind". The thing remembered comes after: *me vino a la memoria su cara*.

English says "I remember" or "it reminds me". Spanish turns it around: the smell or the song does the bringing.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a gustar-type construction: the person is an indirect object and the thing is the subject.

readAndPick.es: Ese olor a tinto me trae recuerdos de mi abuela.
options: That smell of coffee brings back memories of my grandmother.
I bring my grandmother memories of coffee.
My grandmother brings back memories of coffee.

readAndPick.es: De repente me vino a la memoria su cara.
options: Suddenly I forgot her face.
Suddenly her face came to mind.
Suddenly her face came to him.

readAndPick.es: Esta canción le trae muchos recuerdos a don Hernando.
options: This song brings back a lot of memories for Don Hernando.
Don Hernando brings back a lot of memories of this song.
This song brings back a lot of memories for me.

readAndPick.es: Este barrio nos trae buenos recuerdos.
options: This neighbourhood brings back good memories for me.
This neighbourhood brings back bad memories for us.
This neighbourhood brings back good memories for us.
What memories does the café bring back for you?
What memories does the café bring back for him?

Now the name of the street comes to mind.

options: His voice left my mind.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Este barrio ___ trae buenos recuerdos.* (*nos* or *nosotros*) This neighbourhood brings back good memories for us.
yourTurn.answer: Este barrio nos trae buenos recuerdos.
yourTurn.why: The person it happens to is an indirect object: *nos*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Ese olor a tinto me ___ recuerdos de mi abuela.* (*trae* or *traigo*) That smell of coffee brings back memories of my grandmother.
yourTurn.answer: Ese olor a tinto me trae recuerdos de mi abuela.
yourTurn.why: The smell is the subject, so the verb is *trae*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: This song brings back a lot of memories for Don Hernando.
yourTurn.answer: Esta canción le trae muchos recuerdos a don Hernando.
yourTurn.why: *Le* stands for Don Hernando, and *a don Hernando* names him.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Suddenly her face came to mind.
yourTurn.answer: De repente me vino a la memoria su cara.
accept: De repente su cara me vino a la memoria.
yourTurn.why: The thing that came to mind, *su cara*, comes after the verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: What memories does the café bring back for you?
yourTurn.why: *Te* is you, the one it happens to.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Now the name of the street comes to mind.
yourTurn.answer: Ahora me viene a la memoria el nombre de la calle.
accept: Ahora el nombre de la calle me viene a la memoria.
yourTurn.why: *Viene* is present, because the thought is arriving now.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: *Esa foto me trae recuerdos.* becomes: Those photos bring back memories for me.
accept: Esas fotos me traen muchos recuerdos.
yourTurn.why: Plural photos take plural *traen*, and *me* stays.

pitfalls.wrong: Yo traigo recuerdos de mi abuela con el olor.
pitfalls.right: Ese olor me trae recuerdos de mi abuela.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The smell brings the memories, not you: put the smell as the subject.
One thing brings the memories, so the verb is singular.

pitfalls.wrong: Su cara vino a la memoria.
pitfalls.right: Me vino a la memoria su cara.
pitfalls.why: Say who it came to mind for: *me*.

personal: What smell or song takes you back? Say it: *Esa canción me trae recuerdos de…*
